paragraphs: 表情头盔 · 会表情的 AI 员工头像 An expressive, zero-dependency SVG helmet avatar for AI agents.

npface renders a small helmet-shaped face — a deep-navy rounded square helmet, white visor slot, two neon-green rounded-square eyes (the npcrew brand mark, flat 2D) — and makes it emote. Expressions come entirely from the two eyes, the visor and tiny helmet motions: blinks, squint-smiles, wide eyes, side glances, sleepy half-lids, reading saccades, a radar-like "searching" circle, dizzy X-eyes, z z z, nods, head tilts, breathing.
Give it a semantic state name and it takes care of the rest:
features: 13 states: sleep · wake · idle · blink · happy · proud (complete) · thinking · search-docs · search-web · working · waiting · error (dizzy) · sad (tired) — plus aliases (searching, rag, browsing, tired …; searchDocs /…
Zero dependencies, framework-agnostic core (plain SVG/DOM, built-in springs & easing, one shared requestAnimationFrame loop). 9 KB gzip.
React bindings (npface-react): . Vue can follow.
Alive by default: breathing, random glances, auto-blink, per-state rhythm; optional eyes-follow-pointer.
Considerate: pauses off-screen (IntersectionObserver), honours prefers-reduced-motion (static poses + minimal transitions), role="img" + aria-label.

paragraphs: Elftes Stück der Graphen-und-Netzwerke-Reihe der "Konzepte"-Reihe für die Website "Sebastian Hanisch – Operations Research und Machine Learning", ein direktes Kind der Wurzel (Stück 1, bfs-dfs-demo): die Bandbreite B(π) = max über Kanten (u,v) von |π(u)-π(v)| misst, wie weit die Endpunkte jeder Kante in einer Knotennummerierung π auseinanderliegen – zentral beim Lösen großer dünnbesetzter Gleichungssysteme (FEM, Cholesky-Zerlegung): eine schmale Bandbreite hält alle Nicht-Null-Einträge nah an der Diagonale und macht die Zerlegung viel billiger. In den ersten sechs Stücken war alles ein Gut: ein Fluss, ein Preis je Einheit, und Successive Shortest Paths fand den billigsten Fluss. Jetzt fahren mehrere Güter (Frische, Trocken, Kühl, Getränke, Tiefkühl) über dieselben Lanes und…

Einordnung in die Reihe (die Kanten des Graphen): Der Ein-Gut-Fluss ist der Sonderfall K = 1 (Test: gleich dem Optimum von networkx). repositories.description: Variable Neighborhood Search TSP demo - escalating + resetting double-bridge kick strength vs a fixed-strength ILS baseline

paragraphs: Viertes Stück der Trajektorien-Metaheuristiken-Linie der "Konzepte"-Reihe für die Website "Sebastian Hanisch – Operations Research und Machine Learning": dieselbe Rundtour wie in der hill-climbing-demo, der simulated-annealing-demo und der iterated-local-search-demo (ein Depot, n Kundenstopps in einem 100 × 100-km-Gebiet), dieselbe untere Schranke.

Einordnung in die Reihe: Variable Neighborhood Search (VNS, Mladenović & Hansen 1997) baut direkt auf Iterated Local Search auf und löst dessen offene Frage: ILS brauchte eine feste Störstärke (in der Schwester-Demo von Hand kalibriert: 2-3 Doppelbrücken, nicht der literaturübliche Standardwert 1). VNS ersetzt den festen Regler durch ein systematisches Verfahren: die Störstärke $k$ startet bei 1, wächst nach einem erfolglosen Kick und wird nach einem Erfolg auf 1 zurückgesetzt.

Ergebnis in Kürze: mit einer vernünftig gewählten Obergrenze $k{\max}$ schlägt VNS bei JEDEM gemessenen Budget die naive feste Störstärke 1 (oder liegt gleichauf) und den von Hand kalibrierten Sweet Spot (Störstärke 3) bei knappem (10 Tausend) und bei großem Budget (ab 200 Tausend); bei 25 bis 100 Tausend liegt der Sweet Spot vorn. 60 Stopps, 10 Tausend Vorschläge: VNS 1.23 % über der Schranke gegen 1.56 % (Störstärke 1) und 1.35 % (Störstärke 3); bei 200 Tausend: 0.63 % gegen 0.66 % und 0.65 %; bei 25 / 50 / 100 Tausend dagegen VNS 0.85 / 0.80 / 0.77 % gegen 0.81 / 0.74 / 0.68 % (Störstärke…

paragraphs: This is a public initiative aimed at demonstrating that current VPN solutions, such as OpenVPN and WireGuard, are unnecessarily overcomplicated. It turns out that a savvy teenager can write their own VPN protocol with the help of AI.

It opens up incredible possibilities: you can implement the wildest ideas you can think of. For example, you could turn your VPN into a "document transfer" stream by embedding network bytes directly into the structure of a Word file. And that is just one of thousands of potential ideas. Moreover, the uniqueness of your protocol ensures that your VPN’s signatures will be absent from any censorship databases.

We are forming a critical mass of people who know that a VPN is just 200 lines of code. These people will create new breakthrough solutions by the time current protocols are blocked. Of course, we couldn't let these ideas get lost on the 1,778th page of search results, so we update the repository every hour. Even if it looks like spam, it’s our only way to ensure the distribution of this knowledge.

The operation of removing an item is going to be called destack()ing.

repositories.name: aegis-integrity
repositories.description: Free, local-first academic integrity checker and MCP server: citation hallucination detection, AI-text and plagiarism signals, venue guideline checks (IEEE, ACM, Elsevier). Documents never leave your machine.

paragraphs: Real CLI output on a synthetic sample paper (docs/demo/samplepaper.txt). Both DOIs in it are invented, and AEGIS flags them.

1. Local-first processing. AEGIS never uploads your manuscript anywhere -- analysis runs entirely on your own machine. Citation checks may query Crossref/OpenAlex with reference metadata (titles, authors, DOIs), never the document itself, and only when online verification is enabled.

2. Reduced false-positive bias against international researchers. Liang et al. (Stanford, 2023) found GPT detectors misclassified more than half of non-native-authored TOEFL essays as AI-generated. AEGIS applies per-language calibration across 15 languages to reduce this bias.

whatItDoes.text: Real CLI output on a synthetic sample paper (docs/demo/samplepaper.txt). Both DOIs in it are invented, and AEGIS flags them.

repositories.name: llm-xray
repositories.description: See how an LLM works end to end - a live, faithful visualization of a real GPT-2's full forward pass, token by token, from tokenization to sampling.

paragraphs: Live demo: huggingface.co/spaces/swarina/llm-xray · deployment guide in DEPLOY.md (free Space - the first visit after it's idle takes 1 min to wake and load GPT-2)

This isn't a diagram of how language models work - it's the real machine, running. Load a real GPT-2 and watch it generate text one token at a time, with every stage of the forward pass exposed: tokens → embeddings → attention → feed-forward → layer-by-layer prediction → sampling → repeat. Every number on screen comes from the actual model. A detail control scales it from the full forward pass (detailed, the default) down to just "watch it write" (simple).
It began as a fact-check of the article How LLMs actually work and grew into a tool for seeing the pipeline instead of just reading about it.

repositories.name: PosturePro
repositories.description: Real-time posture monitor using MediaPipe Pose that detects neck and torso angles from a webcam and alerts after 3 minutes of poor posture — available as a browser app and a Python desktop app.

paragraphs: Real-time posture detection via computer vision — no backend, no login, just open and sit straight.

PosturePro uses Google's MediaPipe Pose model to track key body landmarks — shoulders, ear, and hip — then computes neck and torso inclination angles in real time. If either angle exceeds the good-posture threshold for more than three minutes, an on-screen warning fires. The tool ships as both a browser app (zero installation, hosted on GitHub Pages) and a Python desktop app for offline use — covering both quick demos and long work sessions with no server costs or sign-up friction.

repositories.name: RIMKit
repositories.description: Robot Intelligence Lab Motion Kit for human-to-humanoid motion retargeting

paragraphs: RIMKit (Robot Intelligence Lab Motion Kit) converts SOMA human motion into whole-body motion for humanoid robots. The current release provides the CoRe method for contact-aware retargeting and bundles seventeen targets from Unitree Robotics, ROBOTIS, Apptronik, LimX Dynamics, Fourier Intelligence, PNDbotics, Booster Robotics, ENGINEAI, Menlo Research, AgiBot, and ROBROS behind one Python and command-line interface, with robot-motion .npz and video export ready out of the box.

Source motions can be supplied as Kimodo .npz files or GEM-X .pt files. RIMKit selects the source adapter from the extension and normalizes both formats to the same SOMA77 stage contract before retargeting.
RIMKit uses the MuJoCo simulator to load robot models, evaluate collision distances, and render motion previews.
features: Contact-aware whole-body retargeting with collision refinement and grounding
One pipeline for seventeen bundled humanoid robot models
Switch robots with a single --robot argument
Compiled C++ MuJoCo kernels with a portable Python fallback
Browser, command-line, and Python interfaces

repositories.name: upi-offline-mesh
repositories.description: Explore this public GitHub project.

paragraphs: A Spring Boot demo of offline-first UPI payments routed through a phone-to-phone mesh network.

You're in a basement with zero signal. You send a friend ₹500. Your phone encrypts the payment and broadcasts it to nearby phones over "Bluetooth." The packet hops device to device until some phone walks outside, picks up 4G, and quietly uploads it to this backend — which decrypts it, checks it hasn't been seen before, and settles it exactly once.
This repo is the server side of that system, plus a built-in simulator of the mesh, so you can run the entire flow on one laptop — no real Bluetooth hardware, no other devices needed.

repositories.description: Scrub the whole crypto market like a video: every symbol, full orderbook + trades + funding, rewound to any moment, reconstructed in O(1) via deterministic re-fold.

paragraphs: Scrub the whole crypto market like a video — every symbol, full orderbook + trades + funding, rewound to any moment, reconstructed in O(1) via deterministic re-fold.

▶ Live demos: the backtester compiled to WebAssembly, an equity curve building bar by bar — backtest-live.wickra.org; one StrategySpec side by side in Python, Rust, JS and Go — playground.wickra.org; all 514 indicators of the core over a real Binance feed — live.wickra.org. Machine folds recorded market feeds from wickra-exchange through the wickra-backtest replay engine, so seeking to any past timestamp reconstructs the exact microstructure state by replaying the events themselves — nothing is interpolated, and no stored state is ever handed back as the answer; the periodic re-fold anchors only bound how far a backward seek has to replay.

repositories.name: jev-benchmark
repositories.description: Benchmarks and a playground for TypeSafe's Jev (System One) model: chess, and who-is-the-player-talking-to for speech-to-text game NPCs

paragraphs: Two hands-on benchmarks of Jev, the "System One" model from TypeSafe. Jev doesn't generate text or reason step by step. You hand it state (a JSON blob) and typed questions (yes/no, pick-one, or rate-on-a-scale) and it returns calibrated probabilities in about 200 ms. The pitch is "programmable common sense": code owns the workflow, Jev supplies the judgment.
I wanted to know where that holds up and where it breaks, so I tested it on two very different tasks:
Everything is here: the code, the labeled data, every raw request and response (runs/raw/), the metrics, and an interactive playground. Model served as jev-1.13.0 on 2026-09-16.
features: Chess – deliberately outside its lane. Chess is calculation and search wearing a judgment costume.

"Who is the player talking to?" – squarely inside its lane. A video game where the player speaks aloud to NPCs through speech-to-text, and the engine must decide which characters should pay attention.

whatItDoes.text: Two hands-on benchmarks of Jev, the "System One" model from TypeSafe. Jev doesn't generate text or reason step by step. You hand it state (a JSON blob) and typed questions (yes/no, pick-one, or rate-on-a-scale) and it returns calibrated probabilities in about 200 ms. The pitch is "programmable common sense": code owns the workflow, Jev supplies the judgment.

repositories.name: dotenv-audit
repositories.description: Audit .env files against an example file or typed schema, compare environments without revealing values, and catch env files committed to git. Zero-dependency Node.js CLI with JSON output and CI exit codes, plus a browser playground.

paragraphs: Audit .env files against an example file or a typed schema, compare environments without revealing values, and catch env files committed to git. A zero-dependency Node.js CLI with CI-friendly exit codes and JSON output.
Try it in your browser: dotenv-audit.netlify.app runs check and diff locally on pasted configuration; nothing is uploaded.

Deployments fail because .env lacks a key that .env.example has, a value has the wrong type (PORT=three-thousand), a placeholder (changeme) shipped to production, or staging and production quietly drifted apart. Teams also commit .env files by accident. dotenv-audit checks all of that from the outside, in CI or before a deploy, and never prints a value while doing it.
features: check an env file against .env.example (missing, empty, unknown and
duplicate keys) and/or a typed JSON schema (string, integer, number, boolean, port, url, email, enum, json with constraints).
Placeholder detection for secret-looking keys (APIKEY=changeme,
diff two env files: keys only in one, keys whose values differ, and how
many are identical. Values are never shown, and there is no flag to show them.

whatItDoes.text: Audit .env files against an example file or a typed schema, compare environments without revealing values, and catch env files committed to git. A zero-dependency Node.js CLI with CI-friendly exit codes and JSON output.

repositories.name: Himmel
repositories.description: A managed, orchestrated harness for running Claude Code as a safe, repeatable agent: hooks, guardrails, slash commands, a Jira CLI, and a cross-session handover system.

paragraphs: 🚀 New here? → Getting Started: from clone to your first PR-gated loop in about 15 minutes. Deciding whether it is worth it? Read Why himmel, the failure modes it exists for and what each one costs. Want the design in one read? System design explains the parts, one ticket's flow, the trust model and the trade-offs. Want the wiring? Architecture draws the enforcement layers, handover, fleet, Jira seam and observability chain.

himmel is a development engine for a solo operator or a small team who works with Claude Code every day. It wraps Claude Code in hooks, guardrails, slash commands, a local Jira CLI and a handover system, so the work follows a worktree-isolated, PR-gated, Jira-tracked workflow without anyone having to remember the rules.

The idea is simple: anything you would otherwise repeat by hand (checking a commit, reviewing a PR, writing down where you stopped, restarting after a usage cap) becomes a tool or a gate. Safety comes from structure, not from Claude remembering a paragraph of instructions.
features: Every feature has one doc that owns its detail; the full map is docs/README.md.
Core loop and enforcement
Worktree isolation with /worktree, /clean, /cleangarden:
docs/commands-catalog.md and CLAUDE.md (## WORKFLOWS)
Pre-commit and Claude tool-call guardrail hooks, and the multi-agent PR

repositories.name: zeocore
repositories.description: A typed capability-authoring framework for Python — write tools that validate input, do their work, and return a structured result.

paragraphs: ZeoCore is a Python framework for writing capabilities: small, typed, named units of work that anything can call.

You write a function once — giving it an identity, a typed request and response, a declaration of its side effects, and a structured result — and that same function can then be run by a script, served over HTTP, exposed to an MCP-native coding agent like Claude Code or Cursor, or handed to an LLM as a callable tool. You don't rewrite it for each destination.
New here? Start with the Quickstart. It takes you from an empty folder to a running capability in about ten minutes, and assumes no prior knowledge of ZeoCore.

repositories.name: cabinet-clear
repositories.description: Explore this public GitHub project.

paragraphs: Understand your discharge letter. Make sense of your medicine cabinet. Know when to ask a pharmacist.

Cabinet Clear is a bilingual, AI-assisted health-literacy application designed to help people understand hospital discharge instructions and organize the medicines they already have at home. It connects information from a discharge letter with medicine-label information, highlights possible discrepancies, and encourages users to confirm uncertain decisions with a pharmacist or healthcare professional.

It's 11 p.m. Maya, 9, is finally asleep after an asthma flare-up. Her dad is sitting at the kitchen table with a discharge letter full of dosing instructions in one hand and a drawer of old inhalers and amoxicillin bottles in the other, trying to figure out which ones are safe to use tonight and which ones have been expired since last winter. Cabinet Clear is built for that exact moment.
features: Trust score. The CNN gives each photo a number between 0 (unclear) and 1 (clear): how confident it is that the photo can be read.

Grad-CAM image. A heat map shows where the CNN looked. If a photo is rejected, you see this map, so you can tell what was wrong (often the expiry date, a small low-contrast stamp) and retake just that shot.

whatItDoes.text: Understand your discharge letter. Make sense of your medicine cabinet. Know when to ask a pharmacist.
